paragraphs: Mentioned in Shabbat 20b and 33b, and Yevamot 97a. Vayikra Rabbah 31:9 has R' Hoshaya, son of R' Shamlai, reporting in his name. Hyman cites Yalkut Tehillim, chapter 19, at the supplied locator תרע״נ, for R' Yehoshua reporting in the name of R' Yitzchak son of R' Zeira.

notes.text: The printed תרע״נ does not justify the previous draft’s number 674. The section number remains unresolved; the final quoted patronymic explicitly gives Rabbi Zeira.

Supplied YalkutTehillim19 תרע״נ remains literal, not the unsupported674 conversion. Earlier finite searches and an unrelated section921 do not identify the passage or prove absence. The first bar Zeira and the final bar R' Zeira are distinct supplied forms; Shamlai is not silently normalized to Simlai. No new whole named paragraph supplies full personal titles, so the abbreviated R' forms are retained. No genealogical authority binding follows from the list.

The consulted sources vary in both title and patronymic. Shabbat 20b has Rav Yitzchak bar Zeira. Shabbat 33b has Rabbi Yitzchak bar Zeiri or Rabbi Shimon ben Nezira, and Yevamot 97a has Rabbi Yitzchak ben Zeira or Shimon Nezira. In Vayikra Rabbah 31:9, Rabbi Hoshaya son of Rabbi Shamlai of Caesarea reports a saying about the setting sun in Yitzchak bar Zeira’s name. The matching Yalkut passage is remez 673, section 4, and it also gives Hoshaya. Hyman’s printed notice (vol. II, p. 791) gives Yehoshua. The matching location and Hyman’s supplied numeral are both recorded.
